findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts:119,158,177 — new sections 6/7/8 create 3 fresh temp project roots via mkdtempSync(...) (each holding a written lattice.config.json) but never clean them up (no rmSync import/call anywhere in the file), unlike ~95% of comparable smoke tasks in packages/main/src/tasks/ (213/223 files using mkdtempSync also call rmSync, e.g. audit-esm-smoke.ts:7,37 which does `rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true })`). Because this file is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands (line 59, focus: fast) and therefore runs on every `lattice validate` invocation going forward, this leaks 3 stray tmpdir directories per run indefinitely — a real, compounding resource-hygiene regression, not a one-off test artifact.

CHK-001:happy:2, CHK-001:edge:2, CHK-001:adversarial:2 (checklist.json) each assert RED/pre-fix ("current main") behavior of validate-command-timeout-smoke.js — exits 1, prints a FAIL line, section 6 fails while sections 1-5 pass. Every one of the 33 bound verificationEvidence entries (all 3 checklist items) carries the IDENTICAL receipt outputDigest 2846ab033bfe46f8813e65938364d2401a95447562c120b1ab694112d88dc37a / outputTail "validate-command-timeout smoke passed: 27 assertions\n" / exitCode 0 — i.e. a GREEN, post-fix run with no FAIL line. A passing-receipt cannot support a failing-state claim: these three intents have zero evidence that the RED state (documented only as a manual stash/rebuild/restore control experiment in plan.md CHK-001 Verify section) was ever captured. Even the checklist items own pinned verification.command/selector for these three intents is the same PASS-selector ("...passed: 27 assertions") smoke invocation, so no red-state proof was ever recorded, only re-confirmations of the current green state.

CHK-002 edge intents E-001 ("Bare-string config entries ... do not inject a spurious timeout"), E-003 ("Shell-style config entries (shell:true) cannot false-positive-match"), E-004 ("Config entry with timeoutMs:0 or negative value" on the NEW pinned-command path), and adversarial A-003/A-004, have NO corresponding check() assertion anywhere in packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts. Grep confirms every validate.commands[] entry ever constructed in the file (lines 126,164,183-184) is object-form {command,args,timeoutMs} with a positive timeoutMs — no bare-string entry, no shell:true entry, and no timeoutMs:0/negative entry is ever written or fed through resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs. These 5 intents are pure code-reading/analytical claims about configuredValidationCommands/commandFromString/resolveCommandTimeoutMs behavior, yet are stamped kind:logic_test, mechanical:true, result:pass, bound to the same shared smoke-run receipt that passes for reasons entirely unrelated to these claims (the 27 assertions that do exist never touch bare-string, shell:true, or zero/negative-timeoutMs config entries).

CHK-002:H-002 ("Diff of checklist.ts shows exactly 4 call sites ... changed ... No duplicated matching logic exists outside the one helper"), CHK-002:H-003 ("git diff HEAD -- packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts produces empty output"), CHK-002:E-005 ("tsc build succeeds ... Import graph is one-way"), and CHK-001:happy:0 ("npm --prefix packages/main run build exits 0") are all bound (per their own verificationIntent.verification.command field in checklist.json) to node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js, NOT to git diff or npm run build. Running the smoke script never invokes git diff or npm run build, so it is circumstantial at best (it would not run if the build were broken) but does not mechanically verify "git diff produces empty output" for the two named files, nor "exactly 4 call sites changed" in checklist.ts, nor does it re-execute npm run build at evidence-capture time. This is the coarse-grained-sharing failure mode the story description explicitly asked to be scrutinized: the shared command is not, for these 4 intents, actually the operation the claim requires.

CHK-001:happy:1 verificationIntent text (checklist.json) still describes plan.md CHK-001 original, pre-CORRECTION single-assertion design: "calls runSingleAllowlistedCommand with the matching command STRING and no options.timeoutMs, and asserts result.timedOut === true and result.code === 124." plan.md line 12-22 explicitly states that design "can NEVER turn green after CHK-002" and documents the CORRECTED split into 6a (validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts:137-138: direct call, no options.timeoutMs, asserts timedOut===false — a permanent characterization, NOT the red->green case) and 6b (lines 147-152: calls resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs then runSingleAllowlistedCommand WITH an explicit {timeoutMs: resolved} option, asserting timedOut===true/code===124). No single call in the implemented file matches happy:1 literal wording (no-options.timeoutMs AND timedOut===true together) — 6a has no-timeoutMs+false, 6b has explicit-timeoutMs+true. The checklist intent text was never updated to reflect the plan CORRECTION even though verificationEvidence for CHK-001:happy:1 is stamped result:pass.
